propositions: The store-wide compaction sweep spawns one fresh `git log --full-history` walk per ticket inside the store write lock, holding all writers stalled for minutes at a time.

Per-ticket position map misses fall through to per-event wildcard walks with leading-wildcard pathspecs (`'*<event-id>*.json'`), defeating pathspec pruning and forcing full-history scans, making deployed cost worse than one-per-ticket.
The `_commit_backfill` function uses unscoped `git add -A` during staging, allowing a concurrent writer's in-flight event files to be swept into the compaction commit.

The sweep never re-yields mid-run: `compact_trigger.run_sweep` probes `write_lock_is_busy` once before starting, and the per-ticket loop in `compact_all_cli` never probes again, forcing writers to wait for the entire run.

The position-keyed `build_position_commit_map` builder maps every event position to its introducing commit in a single pass and is the load-bearing primitive; using the path-keyed sibling `build_introducing_commit_map` would silently miss every lookup and restore per-event walks.
The authorship ledger prep (history walk) must be hoisted out of the critical section and run once per sweep before any lock, then only the SNAPSHOT write, renames, and commit remain under the lock.
